nginx_thn.title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
nginx_thn.lead: A flaw in NGINX's HTTP/2 support can allow an attacker to run code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled, without needing to log in. The decade-old flaw, CVE-2026-123007, dubbed "nginx2root," has been present in NGINX's open-source code since version 1.9.5, released on September 22, 2015. optimizely_krebs.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
optimizely_krebs.lead: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.

http2_thn.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
http2_thn.lead: A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module, mod_http2, can let a remote attacker run code on the server. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, it affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71, released yesterday. pt_thn.title: Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes
pt_thn.lead: Microsoft on Tuesday released patches for a total of 1,259 vulnerabilities spanning its software portfolio, the second consecutive month where the patch volume has exceeded 1,000 flaws. These cover 726 flaws in Windows, 174 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 59 in SQL Server, 53 in Developer Tools, and 27 in SharePoint Server. The patches also include 165 non-Microsoft-issued CVE identifiers.

pt_krebs.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
pt_krebs.lead: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.
